content_blocks.text: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 1. At the launch of the Procurement Act 2023 (the Act) in February 2025 the Government introduced a series of new transparency requirements. Due to the phased rollout of the Transforming Public Procurement Programme (TPP), the Government has now commenced several remaining sections of the Act. This document summarises the remaining transparency regulations, their commencement dates and accompanying implementation support for contracting authorities.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 2. The new elements being commenced are:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: a. Section 69 (Payments compliance notices)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: b. Section 70 (Information about payments under public contracts)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: c. Section 71 (Assessment of contract performance)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: d. Below Threshold Identifiers. This will require contracting authorities to collect and publish supplier identifiers in the below-threshold contract details notice for any supplier awarded a notifiable below-threshold contract.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Legislative Commencement Timings
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 3. Section 69 (publication of Payments Compliance Notices) was commenced on 1 January 2026 (other than in respect of procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers [footnote 1] ), and will be commenced on 1 April 2026 in respect of procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 4. Section 70 (publication of information about payments under public contracts) will be commenced on 1 April 2026 (other than in respect of procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 5. Section 71 (publication of information on contract performance) was commenced on 1 January 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 6. The requirement to include a supplier’s unique identifier in notifiable below threshold contracts will take effect from 1 April 2026 (other than in respect of procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers). The Welsh Government already mandates this requirement via the Procurement (Wales) Regulations 2024.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Legislative Requirements
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Section 69 - Payments Compliance Notices
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: What is a Payments Compliance Notice?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Payments Compliance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 7. The notice reports the contracting authority’s average time taken to pay invoices to suppliers following receipt. This notice demonstrates the contracting authority’s compliance with the implied 30-day payment terms set out in section 68 of the Act. The notice covers a 6-month reporting period.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Payments Compliance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 8. Section 69(3) defines a reporting period. With section 69 being commenced from 1 January 2026, the first reporting period will legally run from 1 January 2026 until 31 March 2026. However, in respect of the publication of their first payments compliance notice, we have recommended contracting authorities cover a reporting period from 1 October 2025 until 31 March 2026. This will ensure a full 6 month comparison with the next reporting period). The second reporting period will be 1 April 2026 until 30 September 2026. Each successive six months is a new reporting period.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Payments Compliance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 9. This timing will differ in respect of a procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Payments Compliance Notice?

content_blocks.text: What is published
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 10. Regulation 38 of the Procurement Regulations 2024 [footnote 2] sets out what the Payments Compliance Notice must include [footnote 3] .
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (a). the contracting authority information,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (b). the dates of the first and the last days of the reporting period to which the payments compliance notice relates,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (c). in respect of sums paid by the contracting authority under public contracts during the reporting period
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (i) the average number of days taken to make those payments, where day 1 is the first day after the invoice day;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (ii) the percentage of those payments which were made, where day 1 is the first day after the invoice day
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: within the period beginning on day 1 and ending with day 30;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: within the period beginning on day 31 and ending with day 60;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: on or after day 61,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (d) in respect of sums which became payable under public contracts during the reporting period, the percentage of those payments which were not made within the reporting period, and
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: (e) a statement of the director or similar officer of the contracting authority who is responsible for the contracting authority’s finances setting out that they approve the payments compliance notice and that person’s name and job title.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Timing of Publication
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 11. The first reporting period legally runs from 1 January 2026 until 31 March 2026. However, to ensure a full six-month reporting period for the first notice, we recommend contracting authorities report on the six-month period from 1 October 2025 until 31 March 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 12. This means contracting authorities will be reporting on the timings of payments made against public contracts during a period prior to section 69 coming into force (i.e. looking back and collecting information on timings of payments from 1 October 2025 onwards).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 13. The first UK17 Payments Compliance Notice must be published between 31 March 2026 and 29 April 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 14. Following that, the reporting period is each successive six months, with the Payments Compliance Notice to be published within 30 days of the last day of the reporting period.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 15. This timing will differ in respect of a procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Digital Implementation
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 16. The notice will be available in the Find a Tender Service (FTS) interface by end of March 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 17. E-Senders will be provided with details of the schema, however E-Sender build will be optional. Contracting authorities should contact their E-Senders to confirm if they plan to support the notice.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: What is contract payment information?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 18. Section 70 sets out the obligations to publish information about payments under public contracts (referred to as “contract payment information” in the Procurement Regulations 2024 [footnote 4] ). It provides that a contracting authority must publish specified information about payments of more than £30,000 (including VAT[^5]) made by the authority under public contracts.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 19. The information is to be published quarterly. This requirement applies to all public contracts procured under the Act in accordance with a procurement procedure that commenced on or after 1 April 2026 [footnote 6] (when section 70 was brought into force [footnote 7] ).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: [^5]; As per section 123(2).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 20. Unlike other transparency requirements, contracting authorities will be able to upload a simple template for all relevant payments made in each quarter, rather than a single notice per payment. This template will be available to download in their buyer area.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 21. In accordance with section 70(4) the publication obligation does not extend to a public contract that is:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: a. a utilities contract awarded by a private utility,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: b. a concession contract,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: c. awarded by a school,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: d. awarded by a transferred Northern Ireland authority, unless it is awarded as part of a procurement under a reserved procurement arrangement or devolved Welsh procurement arrangement, or
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: e. awarded as part of a procurement under a transferred Northern Ireland procurement arrangement.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 22. Additionally, section 70 does not apply to framework agreements (under which no payments are made) nor dynamic markets (which are not public contracts). The requirement to publish contract payment information also does not apply to below-threshold contracts or exempted contracts, which are not public contracts. Section 70 will apply to resulting contracts from framework agreements or dynamic markets if they are above threshold (and therefore a public contract).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 23. Commencement for this section in respect of a procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers will take place separately in the future.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: Valuing contracts
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 24. Where a procurement is divided into lots, it is possible that one or more of the contracts awarded in accordance with that procurement procedure are below the applicable threshold for a public contract, and therefore payments made under those contracts would not be subject to the obligation in section 70.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 25. Worked example: A procurement has a total estimated value of up to £250,000 and is divided into four lots of equal value and a contract awarded for each lot. Each of these contracts is set out in the contract details notice. While the procurement is covered procurement (as the total value is above the relevant threshold amount), the value of each individual contract is below the applicable threshold, so from the point of award onwards these would be classed as below-threshold contracts. As a result, the contracting authority would not be required to publish information in respect of any payments made under any of the contracts in this example.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 26. There is no requirement to group multiple payments below £30,000 paid in respect of the same public contract over the quarter for valuation purposes. So, for example, if a contracting authority makes one payment each month valued at £20,000 (inc. VAT) in respect of the same contract, these do not need to be published as part of the authority’s quarterly contract payment information even though collectively the payments total £60,000 for the quarter. However, individual payments of more than £30,000 including VAT which fall below £30,000 once net of VAT must still be included in the published information.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 27. Regulation 38A [footnote 8] of the Procurement Regulations 2024 sets out what must be published as part of the contact payment information, specifically:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: a. in respect of the contracting authority which made the payment, the authority’s:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: i. name;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: ii. contact postal and email addresses;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: iii. unique identifier;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: b. if different from (a), in respect of the contracting authority which published the contract details notice under section 53 of the Act in respect of the contract under which the payment has been made, the authority’s:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: c. the unique identifier for the procurement - this is the contracting process identifier (OCID) (automatically assigned by the Central Digital Platform (CDP));
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: d. the unique identifier for the contract to which the payment relates (automatically assigned by the CDP and visible on the corresponding UK7 contract details notice);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: e. the name of the supplier to whom the payment was made and the unique identifier for the supplier (automatically assigned by the CDP and visible on the corresponding UK7 contract details notice);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: f. the value of the payment net of VAT;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: g. the date when the payment was made.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 28. Regulation 38A(3) also provides that the unique identifiers for the contract and procurement are not required when no notice relating to the contract has previously been published on the CDP and the identifier is not available.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: Timing of publication
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 29. Section 70 only requires contracting authorities (unless exempt) to publish information about any payment of more than £30,000 (inc. VAT) made under public contracts where the procurement of that contract commenced on or after 1 April 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 30. The contract payment information must be published at least quarterly (within 30 days of each quarter end) on the CDP.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 31. Contracting authorities will not need to publish payments made under public contracts where the procurement of that contract commenced prior to 1 April 2026, irrespective of when the contract is awarded and the payments made.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 32. Section 70 does not apply to previous regime contracts (for example, contracts procured under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, Concession Contracts Regulations 2016, Utilities Contracts Regulations 2016 or the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 33. Of course contracting authorities may voluntarily publish information in respect of such contracts, provided that the minimum level of information required to be published by regulation 38A (as set out above) is available and included for each payment.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 34. For the purposes of section 70 a procurement is commenced before 1 April 2026 if before that date:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: a. a tender notice has been published in accordance with section 21(1), or provided in accordance with section 40(1), of the Act;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: b. a qualifying utilities dynamic market tender notice has been provided in accordance with section 40(1) of the Act;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: c. a transparency notice has been published in accordance with section 44(1) of the Act;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: d. in respect of a contract to be awarded in accordance with a framework (to which none of (a) to (c) applies), the contracting authority has contacted the supplier in order to commence the award of that contract;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: e. a below-threshold tender notice has been published in accordance with section 87(1) of the Act;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: f. a contracting authority has invited the submission of tenders in relation to a regulated below-threshold contract (see section 85(1) of the Act); or
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: g. in respect of a below-threshold contract to which neither (e) nor (f) applies, a contracting authority has contacted a supplier in order to commence the award of that contract
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 35. The first payment submission will technically be due by the 29 July 2026 (i.e. before the end of the period of 30 calendar days beginning with the last day of the first quarter). However, we expect some lag time before the first payments are made under in-scope contracts (i.e. those awarded following a procurement which commenced on or after 1st April 2026). Based on the same period this year only 160 above threshold contracts have been awarded in total across all contracting authorities. Given this it may be some time before individual contracting authorities make payments to which section 70 applies and they are required to publish contract payment information; so there is time for authorities to prepare for this requirement.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 36. Therefore, in time for 1 April 2026 contracting authorities will need to:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: a. review their pipeline to flag procurements due to commence (as per paragraph 34) after 1 April 2026 as in scope (once awarded and payment commence);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: b. update internal processes (where required) to ensure payments can be matched to contracts;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: c. confirm any assurance mechanisms are in place for payments e.g to assure payments are matched correctly and any exempt/sensitive payments are removed before publication;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: d. determine a person(s) responsible for compiling and uploading the contract payment information;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: e. register a nominated person(s) on the CDP and add them as a user to the organisation account.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: 37. Digital functionality will be available on Find a Tender ahead of the publication window opening at the start of July.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
Section 70 - Information about payments under public contracts

content_blocks.text: Section 71 - Contract Performance Notices
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: What is a Contract Performance Notice?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 38. A Contract Performance Notice is a notice that is used to publish the information required to be published under section 71 of the Act. The Contract Performance Notice fulfils two functions:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: a. recording the performance of suppliers against key performance indicators (KPIs) where section 52(1) of the Act applies; and
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: b. recording information relating to particular breaches or failure to perform a public contract except where the breach results in a contract being terminated in full (in which case a contract termination notice must be published which is already in force).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 39. Requirements under section 71 do not apply to private utilities, and requirements under section 71(5) (i.e. recording information relating to particular breaches or failure to perform a public contract) do not apply in relation to a light touch contract.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 40. Regulation 39 of the Procurement Regulations 2024 sets out the information to be published in the contract performance notice when reporting on KPIs under section 71(2). The notice must include
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: a. the contracting authority information;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: b. the title of the procurement;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: c. the unique identifier for the procurement and the public contract (as provided by the platform);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: d. a description of the three KPIs that the contracting authority regards as most material to performance of the contract obligations as at the time the contract performance notice is published;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: e. a statement that the notice is being used to set out the contracting authority’s assessment of performance against the selected KPIs;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: f. information about the identity of the supplier(s) to whom the notice relates;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: g. the contracting authority’s assessment of performance against the selected KPIs in accordance with the ratings set out in regulation 39(5) (as replicated in the below table at paragraph 17); and
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: h. the time period to which the contracting authority’s assessment applies.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 41. Where there has been a breach or failure to perform under a public contract and the notice is being published under section 71(5), the notice must include the information set out in regulation 39(7). In both cases this includes:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: c. the unique identifier for the procurement and the public contract;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: d. information about the identity of the supplier(s) to whom the notice relates;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: e. that section 71(5) of the Act applies and the circumstances giving rise to the application of that section;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: f. a statement that the notice is being published either because the supplier has breached the contract and the breach resulted in one of the events referred to in section 71(3)(b), or because the supplier is not performing a public contract to the contracting authority’s satisfaction; and
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: g. the additional information set out in regulation 39(7)(g)-(m) in respect of the breach or failure to perform (for example, remediation or improvement plans, warning or breach notices), as relevant.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 42. Where a supplier has breached a public contract, the Contract Performance Notice must also set out further information including:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: a. whether the breach resulted in partial termination and the extent to which the contract has been terminated, along with the associated date;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: b. whether the breach resulted in the award of damages or a settlement agreement along with the associated dates;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: c. where there is an award of damages or payment of other monies, the amount of damages or other monies paid and the basis on which this has been awarded (for example, whether in accordance with the public contract, a decision of a court or tribunal, or a negotiated settlement);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: d. where there has been a recorded decision of a court or tribunal finding a breach, a link to the web page where the decision can be accessed, or a copy of the decision (which can be attached to the notice).
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 43. In respect of public contracts procured under the Act, from 1st January 2026 contracting authorities will need to:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: a. In relation to KPIs - Publish a Contract Performance Notice every 12 months and on termination of the contract. The requirement to publish a contract performance notice only relates to where KPIs have been set (i.e. public contracts under the Act above £5m). However Contracting Authorities could publish a Contract Performance Notice as soon as section 71 came into force. Where a contract was commenced before 1st January 2026, the 12 month reporting period starts from the contract start date, rather than the commencement of this section.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: b. In relation to Breach and/or failure to improve performance - Publish a Contract Performance Notice within 30 days of the breach (that has resulted in award of damages, partial termination or settlement agreement), or in the case of poor performance, within 30 days of when the supplier fails to improve performance. This means the earliest a contracting authority may have to publish a contract performance notice in relation to breach or failure to perform would be by 30 January 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 44. The Contract Performance Notice will be available on the Find a Tender Service by 30 January 2026 to enable reporting of breaches.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: 45. Schema details were shared with E-Senders on 15th of December 2025 to allow for use when reporting KPIs.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What is a Contract Performance Notice?

content_blocks.text: Below Threshold Identifiers
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: What does below threshold identifier requirements include?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: 46. There is currently no legislative requirement for contracting authorities to ensure that suppliers are registered on the CDP, or have a unique identifier, when participating in the procurement of a notifiable below-threshold contract, leading to a significant gap in data. Although not currently mandatory, supplier registration is recommended as best practice for below-threshold contracts.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: 47. From 1st April 2026, legislation will require contracting authorities to obtain from suppliers their unique identifier and publish them in the below-threshold Contract Details Notice in respect of any supplier awarded a notifiable below-threshold contract.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: 48. This requirement applies to “notifiable below-threshold” contracts, which are regulated below-threshold contracts with an estimated value, including VAT, of at least:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: a. £12,000 for central government (including NHS bodies)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: b. £30,000 for sub-central authorities
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: 49. To support contracting authorities in collecting supplier identifiers, the Cabinet Office has built a Public Procurement Organisation Number (PPON) lookup tool so contracting authorities can look up suppliers and check if they are registered on the CDP via their buyer portals.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What does below threshold identifier requirements include?

content_blocks.text: What information will suppliers have to provide?
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: 50. Suppliers will have to complete a short five minute registration process and receive a unique identifier and share it with a contracting authority before the authority publishes their Below-Threshold Contract Details Notice.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: 51. This simple registration process will require suppliers to provide the following details:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: a. Organisation name
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: b. Organisation address (there is an option to provide a non-UK address)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: c. Email address
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: d. Companies House or other registry number. If suppliers do not have an existing registry number, a PPON will be generated for them.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: e. SME or VCSE status
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
What information will suppliers have to provide?

content_blocks.text: Timing
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 52. In respect of notifiable below-threshold contracts, from 1st April 2026 contracting authorities will need to:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: a. confirm suppliers have registered on the CDP;
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: b. obtain the supplier’s unique identifier (provided by the CDP);
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: c. publish the supplier’s identifier in below-threshold contract details notices.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 53. The requirement will apply to all below-threshold contract details notices published after 1st April 2026. This means if a contract was awarded on 1st March 2026, but the below-threshold contract details notice was not published until 2nd April 2026, the notice would require the supplier identifier. Therefore, suppliers might need to register after being awarded the contract. (It is anticipated going forward that suppliers would likely register on the CDP during the procurement of the contract, prior to the award of the contract.)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 54. If suppliers are not already registered on the CDP, the contracting authority should direct them to complete the free one-time registration on the CDP . Unlike for public contracts, suppliers will not need to complete the supplier information section[^9] before obtaining their identifier. For notifiable below-threshold contracts they will only be required to complete a basic registration to generate an identifier and share it with contracting authorities.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 55. Contracting authorities can confirm that a supplier is registered using the new PPON search tool available via buyer view and should record the supplier identifier in procurement and finance records alongside the supplier’s name.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 56. From 1st April 2026 suppliers will need to:
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: a. register on the CDP,
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: b. receive a unique identifier, and
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: c. share it with a contracting authority, before the authority publishes their below-threshold contract detail notice.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 57. This registration will only need to be done once and will issue the supplier with a unique supplier identifier, which should be provided to the contracting authority. If a supplier already has a unique identifier because they have previously registered on the CDP, they do not need to re-register and the existing identifier can be used.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 58. Contracting authorities will need to include the unique identifier in any below-threshold contract details notice published from 1st April 2026, so any supplier awarded a relevant contract where it is expected the notice will be published from this date will need to register on the CDP and share their unique identifier with the contracting authority.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 59. To register, suppliers should navigate to Find a Tender Platform and follow required steps. The registration process will require the supplier to provide key organisational information including name, email address, organisation identifier etc. Once registered, the supplier will receive a unique supplier identifier (PPON). When awarded a notifiable below-threshold contract, the supplier must provide this identifier to the contracting authority.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 60. The same unique identifier is then used in respect of all future procurements - whether for public contracts or below-threshold. Suppliers only need to register once. (Note if bidding for a public contract the supplier information section must be completed.)
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 61. Digital functionality will be available on Find a Tender Service by April 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?

content_blocks.text: 62. Validation updates will be sent to E-Senders to allow for expected use by 1st April 2026.
heading_path: What are the new legislative requirements being introduced under the Procurement Act 2023?
